form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Perdue (for himself and Ms. Sinema) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs

form.official-title: To establish in the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency of the Department of Homeland Security a Cybersecurity Advisory Committee.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Cybersecurity Advisory Committee Authorization Act of 2020.

subsection.text: Subtitle A of title XXII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 651 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:
The Secretary shall establish within the Agency a Cybersecurity Advisory Committee (referred to in this section as the Advisory Committee).

paragraph.text: The Advisory Committee may advise, consult with, report to, and make recommendations to the Director, as appropriate, on the development, refinement, and implementation of policies, programs, planning, and training pertaining to the cybersecurity mission of the Agency.

subparagraph.text: The Advisory Committee shall develop, at the request of the Director, recommendations for improvements to advance the cybersecurity mission of the Agency and strengthen the cybersecurity of the United States.

Recommendations agreed upon by subcommittees established under subsection (d) for any year shall be approved by the Advisory Committee before the Advisory Committee submits to the Director the annual report under paragraph (4) for that year.

paragraph.text: The Advisory Committee shall periodically submit to the Director—

subparagraph.text: reports on matters identified by the Director; and
reports on other matters identified by a majority of the members of the Advisory Committee.

The Advisory Committee shall submit to the Director an annual report providing information on the activities, findings, and recommendations of the Advisory Committee, including its subcommittees, for the preceding year.

Not later than 180 days after the date on which the Director receives an annual report for a year under subparagraph (A), the Director shall publish a public version of the report describing the activities of the Advisory Committee and such related matters as would be informative to the public during that year, consistent with section 552(b) of title 5, United States Code.

paragraph.text: Not later than 90 days after receiving any recommendation submitted by the Advisory Committee under paragraph (2), (3), or (4), the Director shall respond in writing to the Advisory Committee with feedback on the recommendation. Such a response shall include—

subparagraph.text: with respect to any recommendation with which the Director concurs, an action plan to implement the recommendation; and
with respect to any recommendation with which the Director does not concur, a justification for why the Director does not plan to implement the recommendation.

paragraph.text: Not less frequently than once per year after the date of enactment of this section, the Director shall provide to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Committee on Homeland Security and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a briefing on feedback from the Advisory Committee.

subparagraph.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of the Cybersecurity Advisory Committee Authorization Act of 2020, the Director shall appoint the members of the Advisory Committee.
The membership of the Advisory Committee shall consist of not more than 35 individuals.

clause.text: The membership of the Advisory Committee shall be geographically balanced and shall include representatives of State and local governments and of a broad range of industries, which may include the following:

subclause.text: Other relevant fields identified by the Director.

clause.text: Not more than 3 members may represent any 1 category under clause (i).

subparagraph.text: The term of each member of the Advisory Committee shall be 2 years, except that a member may continue to serve until a successor is appointed.
The Director may review the participation of a member of the Advisory Committee and remove such member any time at the discretion of the Director.
A member of the Advisory Committee may be reappointed for an unlimited number of terms.

paragraph.text: The members of the Advisory Committee may not receive pay or benefits from the United States Government by reason of their service on the Advisory Committee.

subparagraph.text: The Director shall require the Advisory Committee to meet not less frequently than semiannually, and may convene additional meetings as necessary.
At least one of the meetings referred to in subparagraph (A) shall be open to the public.
The Advisory Committee shall maintain a record of the persons present at each meeting.

Not later than 60 days after the date on which a member is first appointed to the Advisory Committee and before the member is granted access to any classified information, the Director shall determine if the member should be restricted from reviewing, discussing, or possessing classified information.
Access to classified materials shall be managed in accordance with Executive Order No. 13526 of December 29, 2009 (75 Fed. Reg 707), or any subsequent corresponding Executive Order.
A member of the Advisory Committee shall protect all classified information in accordance with the applicable requirements for the particular level of classification of such information.

paragraph.text: The Advisory Committee shall select, from among the members of the Advisory Committee—

subparagraph.text: a member to serve as chairperson of the Advisory Committee; and
a member to serve as chairperson of each subcommittee of the Advisory Committee established under subsection (d).

paragraph.text: The Director shall establish subcommittees within the Advisory Committee to address cybersecurity issues, which may include the following:

subparagraph.text: Information exchange.
Critical infrastructure.
Risk management.
Public and private partnerships.

paragraph.text: Each subcommittee shall meet not less frequently than semiannually, and submit to the Advisory Committee for inclusion in the annual report required under subsection (b)(4) information, including activities, findings, and recommendations, regarding subject matter considered by the subcommittee.

The chair of the Advisory Committee shall appoint members to subcommittees and shall ensure that each member appointed to a subcommittee has subject matter expertise relevant to the subject matter of the subcommittee.

subsection.text: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the Advisory Committee and its subcommittees.
